domain: High-Performance Computing Metrics and Performance Analysis
scenario:
A leading technology company is developing an enterprise-grade performance analysis and benchmarking platform to optimize the efficiency and capability of high-performance computing (HPC) systems. The platform aims to collect, process, and analyze various computational metrics from different computing nodes and clusters across the organization's data centers.

The system will track a wide range of performance metrics such as floating-point operations per second (FLOPs), integer operations per second (IOPs), and matrix operations for different data types (e.g., BF16, F16, F32). It will also handle metrics in various units, report peak performance capabilities, and calculate the percentage of peak performance (PoP) achieved during computational tasks.

The platform should support real-time data collection and historical data analysis, enabling IT administrators and engineers to identify bottlenecks, optimize resource allocation, and improve overall system performance. The system must also feature advanced visualization tools for trend analysis and reporting, facilitating data-driven decision-making.

Additionally, the platform will incorporate a robust user management system to regulate access based on roles, such as system administrators, performance analysts, and software engineers. The platform will provide tools for setting benchmark tests, analyzing results, and generating automated performance reports. It will also allow integration with third-party tools for extended functionality, ensuring adaptability to future technological advancements.
